header: Francesca’s came to us at a moment of transition. Their audience, girls navigating early adolescence, was changing fast. What they needed was not just a visual update but a shift in tone. Together, we reimagined the brand as a trusted older sister. Someone stylish, confident, and just gentle enough to guide without pushing.

layout.title: Time for a change
text: Francesca’s was ready for change. Originally built for younger girls, the brand no longer resonated with its growing audience. Their customers, girls aged eleven to fifteen, had become more style aware and were gravitating toward brands like Madewell and Asos. Francesca’s needed a refresh that could evolve with them without leaving their parents behind.
We developed a new direction that balanced trend forward design with approachability. It tested well across audiences. Stylish but not intimidating. Fresh but still familiar.

layout.title: The Strategy
text: To bring that balance to life, we rethought the entire experience. Inspired by fashion magazines, we introduced an editorial layer to the shopping journey. Product pairings were surfaced through moments of suggestion rather than promotion. It felt curated, not prescriptive. Like getting advice from someone just a step ahead.

We validated the concept with users and it quickly became the most popular feature in testing. From there, we built a custom content system that gave the Francesca’s team full control over editorial updates and pairings.
Beyond the rebrand, we also optimized the checkout experience. We tested multiple flows with users, then partnered with the Francesca's team to A B test the top performers.

This work gave Francesca's more than just a new look. It repositioned the brand for a new generation while respecting the one that came before. What began as a rebrand became a more thoughtful way to connect. Style advice delivered with care, confidence, and just the right amount of influence.
